root_idea.summary: A root oriented toward covering, concealing, or preventing clear perception.
root_idea.development: The basic notion of covering develops into loss of physical sight, inward blindness or deviation from guidance, and the obscuring of information or meaning. Related Classical uses extend the covering image to clouds, darkness, foam, and trackless terrain.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form.
Displayed under the normalized Form II perfect citation form, while retaining its Quranic passive usage in the sense description.
Displayed as the adjective and substantivized noun أَعْمَى.
Displayed as the distinct verbal noun عَمًى.
This is the Quranic plural عَمُونَ, explicitly supported as a plural of أَعْمَى, so it is subsumed under that public adjective/noun.

senses.definition: To be or become blind, losing physical sight.
senses.usage_conditions: Used as a Form I verb of becoming or being blind; Quranic usage can concern sight or perception more generally.

senses.definition: To be blind to guidance, truth, or the right course; to err through lack of inward perception.
senses.usage_conditions: A figurative use concerning the mind or heart rather than the eyes, including failure to recognize the right way.

senses.definition: To become obscure or unintelligible to someone.
senses.usage_conditions: Especially in the construction عَمِيَ عَلَيْهِ, with information, affairs, speech, or pleas becoming unapparent or doubtful to the person concerned.

senses.definition: To be made obscure or unintelligible to someone.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is passive and occurs in the construction عُمِّيَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ, describing something made unapparent or unclear to its hearers.

senses.definition: Blind; lacking physical sight, also used substantively for a blind person or the blind.
senses.usage_conditions: The form functions adjectivally and substantively; Quranic occurrences include singular and plural forms.

senses.definition: Blind in mind or heart; unable to perceive guidance or the way to safety.
senses.usage_conditions: A figurative Quranic use concerning inward perception and guidance, including the contrast between blindness and seeing.

senses.definition: Blindness; loss of physical sight or inward perception.
senses.usage_conditions: A verbal noun of عَمِيَ; Quranic usage permits physical or figurative blindness according to context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To betake oneself or direct oneself toward something, without desiring another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction with إِلَى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of waves, to cast particles, rubbish, or foam onto their upper parts; of a camel, to cast mouth-foam onto its head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized physical use describing the upward casting or covering action of waves and a braying camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cast upon someone a suspicion of something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic causative-looking construction with بِـ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of water or another substance, to flow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct intransitive use, also compared with هَمَى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of vegetation, to reach full height, blossom, and become luxuriant or dense.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal or specialized use applied to plants or herbage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render someone physically blind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II causative use, explicitly including blindness of both eyes in the cited definition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To find someone to be blind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV use distinct from the Form II causative, with the object judged or discovered to be blind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feign blindness or pretend not to know something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May concern physical sight or, figuratively, feigned ignorance of a matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To choose, select, or prefer something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical use explicitly equated with اِخْتَارَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To tend, betake oneself, or direct one's aim toward someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A related but distinct use explicitly equated with قَصَدَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Blindly or without insight, especially in undertaking an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the idiom رَكِبَ أَمْرًا عَلَى العَمَى, meaning to embark on a matter without clear knowledge or guidance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Stature or height.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use illustrated in praise of a person's height.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical synonym of غُبَارٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Remoteness or distance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in a poetic description of an object seen from afar.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A chosen, selected, or preferred thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantive derived from اِعْتَمَى in the sense of choosing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Cloud, especially a dense or covering mass of cloud.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term has several Classical descriptions, including lofty, dense, smoke-like, raining, thin, black, or white cloud.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The fiercest midday heat of the hot season.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed expression for the time when the heat is so intense that it dazzles or nearly blinds; associated variants and proper-name explanations do not alter the idiomatic meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Stubborn persistence, contentious wrangling, or litigation in a false or futile matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative noun related to persistence in disputation; it is equated with لَجَاجٌ in the cited usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ignorance or a state of not knowing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An alternative lexical interpretation of the same nominal family in the cited expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A remaining portion of night-darkness; also dimness of the eyes from tears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use describing residual darkness or impaired visual clarity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An obscure or unfounded claim to relationship.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression دَعْوَةٌ عَمْيَاءُ, an obscure claim of kinship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The point or condition of death.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression تَرَكْنَاهُمْ عُمَّى, meaning that they were left at the point of death.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Trial, punishment, slaughter, civil conflict, or factional strife.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun of the measure فِعِّيلَى with several related conflict and ordeal applications.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slain person whose killer is unknown.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed legal and social expression for an unidentified homicide.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pride, self-magnification, error, or deviation from what is right.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the expression concerning a banner of عِمِّيَّة, it refers to factional conflict founded on pride, error, or partisanship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who does not see or recognize the road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A description of someone unable to find the way.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of land, having its traces effaced or obliterated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to land whose former signs or features have disappeared.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having very little milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized epithet explicitly applied to a woman in the cited lexical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Casting or throwing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use applied to a man and equated with رَامٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A torrent and a destructive fire, or other paired forces that spare no place or object.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative dual expression based on the perplexity and indiscriminate force associated with blindness; variants include a torrent and night or an excited camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A partisan or factional affair whose manner of proceeding cannot be distinguished.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed figurative description of a case driven by partisanship or ʿasabiyyah without a discernible right course.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land or a place in which one cannot be directed to the right course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description of terrain or a place that gives no reliable guidance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Trackless tracts of land with no sign of a way, habitation, cultivation, or their traces.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural or collective noun for desolate, bewildering terrain; it may also be understood as مَجَاهِلُ, places of wandering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Tall men.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct plural use, explicitly derived from a word meaning tall.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A verse or saying whose meaning has been made obscure or difficult to understand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial noun describing an enigmatic utterance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The lion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized lexical item with no Quranic occurrence in the supplied form groups.

cautions: The Quranic uses of أَعْمَى and related forms can distinguish physical blindness from blindness of the heart or loss of guidance; some occurrences allow both dimensions in context.
The Form II Quran occurrence is passive and constructional, meaning that something was made obscure to its hearers; it should not be reduced to the physical causative sense alone.
